newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P views Japan bank debentures, deposits as equal.
newsitem.headline: S&P views Japan bank debentures, deposits as equal.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Wednesday that Japanese bank debentures from a credit rating standpoint should be assessed in the same way as deposits and other senior debt.

The view is supported by the fact that bank debentures have equal status with other senior debt under Japanese civil law and would be subject to pro-rata distribution in the event of bankruptcy, S&P said in a statement.

S&P announced the view amid growing investor concern about the status of bank debentures vis-a-vis other senior debt, particularly deposits, as the difference in credit quality among banks widens, S&P said.
Deposit insurance protection does not ensure that deposits will be given priority over other senior debts, as the insurance does not guarantee full and timely debt repayment, S&P said.

S&P said that it should be noted that the regulators' commitment to protect holders of senior debt does not necessarily apply to other types of debts. S&P categorizes subordinated debt and preferred stock below deposits and other senior debt obligations, such as debentures.
Regulators are said to be considering a proposal to have deposit insurance cover bank debentures as well as regular bank deposits.
